We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={z}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=2z, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}=4{e}^{2z}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z=4\int {e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z=2{e}^{2z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =({z}^{2}+1)(2{e}^{2z})-\int (2{e}^{2z})(2z)\,\text{d}z \\  & =2({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}-4\int z{e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int z{e}^{2z}\text{d}z.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=z\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}={e}^{2z}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z=\int {e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z=\frac{{e}^{2z}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int z{e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =(z)(\frac{{e}^{2z}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2z}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{z{e}^{2z}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{z{e}^{2z}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2z}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z & =2({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}-4\int z{e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =2({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}-4(\frac{z{e}^{2z}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2z}}{4}+D) \\  & =2({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}-2z{e}^{2z}+{e}^{2z}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-4D.$ 

Finally, then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}4({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}\,\text{d}z & =(2({z}^{2}+1){e}^{2z}-2z{e}^{2z}+{e}^{2z}){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(2({1}^{2}+1){(e)}^{2}-2(1)^{2}{e}^{2}+{e}^{2})-(2(0+1){e}^{0}-2\cdot 0\cdot {e}^{0}+{e}^{0}) \\  & =3{e}^{2}-3\end{aligned}
$$
